q.t: How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
q.e: ‘Quadri’ means four.

q.t: The four angles of a quadrilateral add up to:
q.e: A diagonal cuts it into two triangles, each with 180°.

q.t: A quadrilateral with four equal sides and four right angles is a:
q.e: Equal sides alone give a rhombus; right angles alone give a rectangle; both give a square.

q.t: In a rectangle, each angle is:
q.e: ‘Rect-angle’ means right angle.

q.t: How many diagonals does a quadrilateral have?
q.e: Each joins a pair of opposite corners.

q.t: A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel is a:
q.e: That is how a parallelogram is defined.

q.t: A parallelogram with all four sides equal is a:
q.e: A rhombus is a ‘pushed-over’ square.

q.t: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides is a:
q.e: Only one pair is parallel.

q.t: How many vertices does a quadrilateral have?
q.e: One at each corner.

q.t: The opposite sides of a rectangle are:
q.e: A rectangle is a special parallelogram.

q.t: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90°, 90° and 100°. Find the fourth (in degrees).
The diagonals of a rectangle are:
q.e: Each is the long side of a right triangle with the same two sides.

q.t: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at:
q.e: All four sides are equal, so each diagonal is the perpendicular bisector of the other.

q.t: Find the perimeter of a square of side 6 cm (in cm).
q.e: Four equal sides.

q.t: Find the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm (in cm).
q.e: Two lengths and two breadths.

q.t: One angle of a parallelogram is 70°. Find the opposite angle (in degrees).
q.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.

q.t: One angle of a parallelogram is 70°. Find an adjacent angle (in degrees).
q.e: Neighbouring angles of a parallelogram add to 180°.

q.t: A quadrilateral with two pairs of equal ADJACENT sides is a:
q.e: In a kite the equal sides are next to each other.

q.t: Is every square a rectangle?
o: Yes — it has four right angles
No — it is a rhombus instead
q.e: A rectangle only needs four right angles; a square has them, plus equal sides.

q.t: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 : 4. Find the smallest (in degrees).
q.e: 10 parts make 360°, so one part is 36°.

q.t: The angles of a quadrilateral are x°, 2x°, 3x° and 4x°. Find the largest (in degrees).
Three angles of a quadrilateral are 110°, 85° and 75°. Find the fourth (in degrees).
One angle of a parallelogram is 3 times its adjacent angle. Find the larger angle (in degrees).
q.e: x + 3x = 180, so x = 45 and the larger is 135.

q.t: A rhombus has perimeter 48 cm. Find its side (in cm).
q.e: Four equal sides.

q.t: A rectangle has perimeter 50 cm and length 15 cm. Find its breadth (in cm).
q.e: Length + breadth = half the perimeter = 25.

q.t: A parallelogram has perimeter 36 cm and one side 10 cm. Find the adjacent side (in cm).
q.e: Two adjacent sides make half the perimeter: 18 − 10.

q.t: Which statement is NOT always true?
q.e: A rhombus has equal sides but its angles need not be 90°.

q.t: All four angles of a quadrilateral are equal. Find each (in degrees).
The diagonals of a square:
o: Are equal and cross at right angles
q.e: A square is both a rectangle (equal diagonals) and a rhombus (perpendicular diagonals).

q.t: The diagonals of a rectangle are 10 cm long. How far is the point where they cross from each corner (in cm)?
q.e: They are equal and cut each other in half.

q.t: The angles of a quadrilateral are (x + 10)°, (2x − 20)°, (x + 30)° and (2x + 10)°. Find the largest angle (in degrees).
A rectangle has length and breadth in the ratio 3 : 2 and perimeter 60 cm. Find its length (in cm).
q.e: Length + breadth = 30 cm, shared 3 : 2 → 18 cm and 12 cm.

q.t: One angle of a rhombus is 60°. Find its largest angle (in degrees).
q.e: Adjacent angles add to 180°, so the angles are 60°, 120°, 60°, 120°.

q.t: Two adjacent angles of a parallelogram differ by 30°. Find the larger (in degrees).
q.e: They add to 180 and differ by 30: 105° and 75°.

q.t: A 2 × 2 grid of small squares is drawn. How many rectangles (including squares) can be found in it?
q.e: The grid has 3 horizontal and 3 vertical lines. Choose 2 of each: 3 × 3 = 9 (four small, four made of two, one large).

q.t: Three angles of a quadrilateral are equal and the fourth is 60°. Find each of the equal angles (in degrees).
q.e: The three share 300° equally.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a kite have?
q.e: Only the diagonal that runs between the two pairs of equal sides.

q.t: In an isosceles trapezium each angle on the longer parallel side is 65°. Find each angle on the shorter parallel side (in degrees).
q.e: The two angles along each slant side add to 180°.

q.t: A square and a rhombus have the same side. Which statement is true?
o: They always have the same area
q.e: Perimeter depends only on the sides (4 × side). The rhombus leans over, so its height and area are smaller.

q.t: Three angles of a quadrilateral are right angles. Find the fourth (in degrees).
q.e: 360 − 270 = 90. So a quadrilateral can never have exactly three right angles — the fourth is forced to be one too.
